definitions.explanation: A conjunction pattern meaning "not only A but also B." Indicates that the scope extends beyond A to include B as well. Often paired with ～も at the end of the clause.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}だけでなく{中国語|ちゅうごくご}も{話|はな}せる。
examples.english: I can speak not only Japanese but also Chinese.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}は{味|あじ}がいいだけでなく、{値段|ねだん}も{手頃|てごろ}だ。
examples.english: This restaurant not only tastes good but is also reasonably priced.

examples.japanese: {運動|うんどう}は{体|からだ}にいいだけでなく、{精神的|せいしんてき}なストレスの{解消|かいしょう}にも{役立|やくだ}つ。
examples.english: Exercise is not only good for the body but also helps relieve mental stress.

notes:
～だけでなく means "not only A but also B." It is one of the most commonly used conjunction patterns for expanding the scope of a statement.

COMMON PATTERNS:
A + だけでなく + B + も
The B clause typically ends with も to emphasize the addition.

CONNECTION FORMS:
- After nouns: {学生|がくせい}だけでなく
- After i-adjectives: {高|たか}いだけでなく
- After na-adjectives: {静|しず}かなだけでなく
- After verbs: {読|よ}むだけでなく

VARIATIONS (FORMAL → CASUAL):
- ～のみならず (formal/written)
- ～ばかりでなく (slightly literary)
- ～だけではなく (slightly more formal than だけでなく)
- ～だけでなく (standard)
- ～だけじゃなく (casual spoken)

USAGE:
In conversation, ～だけじゃなくて (with て) is also very common.
